div.head: ECf 11.1 A 2
div.ab: Debet uero de iure rex omnes terras et honores, omnes dignitates et iura et libertates corone regni huius in integrum cum omni integritate et sine diminutione obseruare et defendere, dispersa et dilapidata et amissa regni iura in pristinum statum et debitum uiribus omnibus reuocare.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 635 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

note.seg: wörtlich deckt sich dies, wie 11, 1 A 9 citirt, mit einem Krönungseid [‘possibly that of Edward I.’ (Stubbs Constit. hist. II 105, ebenso Pollock and Maitland HEL. I 366)]: Il gardera toutez ses terres, honours et dignitees droitturelx et franks del coron du roialme d’Englitere en tout maner d’entierte sans nul maner d’amenusement; et les droites disperges, dilapides ou perdus de la corone a son pouoir reappeller en l’auncien estate. Vgl. auch Lond in 13, 1 A 1 ff. und Fleta I 8: antiqua maneria uel iura coronæ annexa regi non licebit alienare, sed omnis rex coronæ suæ alienata reuocare tenetur. Vielleicht stand die Forderung im Programm der Staatsreformer nach Richards I. Zeit, in dessen Eid sie noch fehlt

this corresponds word for word, as 11, 1 A 9 cites it, with a coronation oath [‘possibly that of Edward I.’ (Stubbs, Constit. hist. II 105; likewise Pollock and Maitland, HEL. I 366)]: Il gardera toutez ses terres … en l’auncien estate. Cf. also Lond at 13, 1 A 1 ff. and Fleta I 8: antiqua maneria … reuocare tenetur. Perhaps the demand stood in the programme of the reformers of the state after the time of Richard I, in whose oath it is still missing
